description.p: This is a community package of OpenLogi: it repackages the official upstream Debian build unmodified, fetched from upstream's releases at install time.

OpenLogi is a native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+. It remaps buttons, sets DPI, tunes SmartShift, and applies per-application profiles to Logitech HID++ devices: over a Bolt or Unifying receiver, over Bluetooth, or wired. There is no account and no telemetry; configuration is a plain TOML file.

ul.li: Remap buttons, including gesture and Actions Ring bindings
Set DPI and cycle between DPI presets
Per-application profiles that switch on the focused window

description.p: One setup step is needed after installing: device nodes are owned by root, so OpenLogi's udev rules have to be installed on the host, which a Flatpak cannot do itself. Until then no devices are listed. Run this once in a terminal, then unplug and replug the receiver or device and restart the app:

p.code: flatpak run --command=cat org.openlogi.OpenLogi /app/share/openlogi/udev/70-openlogi.rules | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/70-openlogi.rules >/dev/null && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger

description.p: The app's Settings, Permissions page shows whether access is granted.

The "Launch at login" setting has no effect in this package: it registers a systemd user service, which the sandbox cannot reach. Button remapping and per-application profiles run in OpenLogi's background agent, which starts when you open the app, so open OpenLogi once after logging in.
